In the darkest shades on this map, up to roughly 1 in 10 newborns won't reach age five. In the palest, well under 1 in 200. Same planet, same year.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The map shows the estimated share of newborns who die before turning 5, for 2024. Data: Our World in Data (CC BY). The scale runs from under 0.2% to over 20%.
2/ WHO estimates about 4.9 million children under five died worldwide in 2024. In 1990 the figure was around 12.6 million, even though the world had far fewer people.
3/ The global rate fell from about 93 deaths per 1,000 births in 1990 to roughly 36 in 2020, a drop near 60%. Few big global indicators have improved this far, this fast.
4/ The red belt on the map runs across sub-Saharan Africa, with Pakistan and Afghanistan also in the darker bands. Somalia is generally cited as having the highest rate.
5/ Size matters too. Nigeria, India, Pakistan, DR Congo, Ethiopia and China together account for roughly half of all under-5 deaths, because they combine large populations with uneven rates.
6/ Pneumonia, preterm birth complications, diarrhea and malaria feature heavily, with undernutrition a major underlying factor. Many of these deaths are preventable with cheap, proven care.
7/ Which part of this map do you expect to change most by 2035? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
